page: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-128 is a memory-optimized instance engineered for exceptionally large, memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.6 GHz, the server delivers 128 dedicated virtual CPUs across 64 physical cores with two threads per core. The architecture features an extensive 1952.0 GB pool of system memory, yielding 15.25 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions alongside dedicated cryptographic modules such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The platform provides no local storage and does not bundle hardware GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring reliance on attached network block storage.

Benchmark results reflect the massive parallel compute and memory scale of the configuration. Multi-threaded evaluations highlight strong performance, with multi-core stress-ng scores reaching 120,736.75 and Geekbench multi-core hitting 17,468.0. In memory throughput testing, read bandwidth delivers 6,507.69 GB/sec on cached blocks and 298.49 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads, complementing write bandwidth of 122.84 GB/sec. The instance demonstrated top-tier performance in CPU encryption (104,535.88) and Geekbench ray tracing (105,464.0), paired with strong results in PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations exceeding 106 million operations per second. Conversely, single-thread stress-ng and Geekbench single-core metrics sit squarely in the mid-tier category.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m3-megamem-128 aggregates immense memory capacity and dedicated core density on a single node, minimizing infrastructure overhead for workloads that exceed standard virtual machine memory limits. The lack of hardware accelerators makes it poorly matched for generative AI execution, as reflected by weak large-model text generation rates of 2.73 tokens per second. Instead, the balance of hardware capabilities aligns with large-scale in-memory databases, real-time analytics caches, massive relational database operations, and high-concurrency enterprise software compilation.
description: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-128 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz across 64 physical cores, accompanied by 1952.0 GB of memory. It includes no bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on remote block storage for persistence. In benchmark testing, the platform exhibits strong multi-core processing, top-tier cryptographic execution, and high memory bandwidth, achieving over 106 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database scores. Single-threaded metrics and CPU-based large language model generation remain modest. Given its 15.25 GB memory-to-core allocation, m3-megamem-128 represents a specialized platform for in-memory databases, large data caches, relational database systems, and heavy parallel compilation.
